raw_case_text:
The patient's medical history included recurrent acute otitis media and seasonal allergic rhinitis (AR), both beginning when he was 5 years-old. He was diagnosed with bronchial asthma (BA) when he was 6 years old, when AR became continuous and severe. He lived with his parents and younger brother, all of whom exhibited BA and pollinosis. There were no pets or smokers in his house.
On physical examination, the patient appeared to be well. His weight was 21.9 kg (- 1.0 SD) and his height was 126.6 cm (- 0.2 SD). His vital signs were as follows: pulse rate, 81 beats per minute; respiratory rate, 20 breaths per minute; temperature, 37.0  C; and oxygen saturation, 99% while breathing ambient air. Examination of the chest revealed prolonged expirations, sibilant rhonchi, and coarse crackles on the right side. Spirometry showed a forced vital capacity of 92%, a 1-s forced expiratory volume of 64%, and poor reversibility upon inhalation of a beta stimulant.
Hematological and serum biochemical examinations revealed a white blood cell count of 8600/muL, with a differential profile of 23% eosinophils, and a serum total IgE level of 151 IU/mL. ImmunoCAP tests for IgEs produced in response to Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus, Aspergillus, Candida, Alternaria, Cladosporium, and other common allergens were all negative.
Eosinophilia, bilateral nasal polyps, and pansinusitis were observed via computed tomography (Fig. 1), and the diagnosis was severe refractory BA associated with ECRS. The patient received oral prednisolone (PSL, 10 mg/day), which alleviated both the BA and nasal symptoms. However, during tapering of the steroid, the symptoms soon recurred, and nasal-opening surgery (endoscopic sinus surgery) was performed half a year later. After surgery, the BA was controlled during PSL dose reduction, but 4 months after surgery, the nasal polyps recurred and an eosinophilic infiltrate was found in the extracted nasal polyps (Fig. 2). Therefore, PSL at 10 mg/day was continued.

subjective.chief_complaint: A school-aged boy presented with severe corticosteroid-dependent bronchial asthma and chronic pansinusitis with recurrent bilateral nasal polyposis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed recurrent acute otitis media and seasonal allergic rhinitis at age 5, which progressed at age 6 to continuous severe allergic rhinitis and refractory bronchial asthma. Although oral prednisolone (10 mg/day) controlled his asthma and nasal symptoms, symptoms rapidly relapsed upon steroid tapering, and bilateral nasal polyps recurred 4 months after endoscopic sinus surgery.
subjective.past_medical_history: Recurrent acute otitis media and allergic rhinitis since age 5; bronchial asthma since age 6. Family history positive for bronchial asthma and pollinosis in his parents and younger brother; no household pets or tobacco smoke exposure.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for chronic nasal obstruction/polyposis, wheezing, and cough.

objective.physical_examination: Well-appearing child; weight 21.9 kg (-1.0 SD), height 126.6 cm (-0.2 SD), pulse 81 bpm, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, temperature 37.0 C, and room-air SpO2 99%. Chest auscultation revealed prolonged expiration, sibilant rhonchi, and right-sided coarse crackles.
objective.routine_investigations: Spirometry demonstrated airflow obstruction with FVC 92% predicted, FEV1 64% predicted, and poor bronchodilator reversibility. Blood tests showed WBC 8,600/uL with marked peripheral eosinophilia (23% eosinophils) and serum total IgE of 151 IU/mL. ImmunoCAP allergen-specific IgE testing was negative for Dermatophagoides pteronyssinus, Aspergillus, Candida, Alternaria, Cladosporium, and other common inhalant allergens.
objective.advanced_workup: Paranasal sinus CT demonstrated bilateral nasal polyps and pansinusitis. Histopathological examination of nasal polyps resected during endoscopic sinus surgery confirmed dense mucosal eosinophilic infiltration.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Pediatric severe refractory bronchial asthma associated with eosinophilic chronic rhinosinusitis (ECRS) and recurrent eosinophilic nasal polyposis, confirmed by peripheral eosinophilia (23%), sinus CT showing bilateral polyposis and pansinusitis, and polyp histopathology demonstrating dense eosinophilic infiltration; allergic bronchopulmonary mycosis/aspergillosis and IgE-mediated fungal sensitization were excluded by negative ImmunoCAP specific IgE to Aspergillus, Candida, Alternaria, and Cladosporium. Managed with endoscopic sinus surgery and maintenance low-dose oral prednisolone (10 mg/day) after polyp recurrence 4 months postoperatively.
